statement: Availability-aware execution activates when the snapshot declares any membership, sessions, trading_status or lifetime family, or when the experiment supplies a valuation policy; a corporate-action family alone does not activate it.
notes: Experiment-construction overlap with subsystem 2 (reader A); integrator to dedupe.

statement: An active experiment refuses without a declared sessions family (ledgr_availability_sessions_required) and without a schema-2 ledgr_valuation_stale() policy (ledgr_valuation_policy_required); there is no default stale horizon.
notes: Schema-1 valuation policies refuse with a reconstruct message (availability-policy.R:172-180).

statement: ledgr_universe_members(id) must name a membership scope declared by the snapshot (ledgr_membership_universe_not_found); a membership rule on a snapshot without availability families refuses with ledgr_availability_inactive.
oddity: The inactive-snapshot message says the rule needs membership and session facts, but activation is triggered by any one runtime family or a valuation policy.

statement: A character-vector universe under active availability is a fixed basket: the provider's members are the declared IDs in declared order at every pulse, whatever the membership facts say; status and lifetime facts still restrict them.
Under a membership rule the physical instrument axis of the fold is every snapshot instrument; members are resolved per pulse from it.
notes: Bars, features and positions are held for all snapshot instruments, including never-members such as the fixture's JJJ and KKK2.

statement: A membership, status or lifetime row applies at cutoff t only when max(effective_from, knowledge_time) <= t < effective_to (half-open; missing effective_to is open-ended; missing times never apply).

Membership sets: a header becomes eligible once effective and knowable; eligible headers are ordered by (effective_from, knowledge_time, set_id); the last eligible complete set resets membership and members are the union of that set and every later eligible set.
notes: Order is by effective time, not knowledge time: a late-known complete set with an earlier effective_from does not displace an already applicable set with a later effective_from.

statement: Interval membership assertions applicable at t override the set-derived state of their instrument, and among several applicable intervals for one instrument the last in (effective_from, knowledge_time, fact_id) order wins.
oddity: An open-ended interval assertion keeps an instrument a member even after a later complete set omits it (provider and resolver agree).
notes: Whether one universe may mix sets and intervals is an ingest question (subsystem 1).

statement: Runtime membership is two-valued: an instrument with no applicable membership evidence is a nonmember, while ledgr_facts_resolve() reports the same case as member = NA with reason unknown_no_usable_evidence.
oddity: Two membership resolvers exist (prepared runtime closure and ledgr_membership_resolve_at); they differ in how unknown is represented.
notes: BBB at the s9 close (announced s5 17:15 ET; effective s10 open): provider nonmember; resolver NA.

statement: For a membership rule the decision axis is the members in C-locale stable-ID order followed by held nonmembers in the same order; for a fixed basket it is the declared order followed by held nonmembers.

Any nonzero position (either sign) on an instrument that is not a current member puts it on the decision axis as a held nonmember, including instruments that were never universe members (for example spin-off recipients).
notes: JJJ (never a member) held appears on the axis with status_unknown under the fixture's status family.

statement: Trading status at t: applicable rows superseded by another applicable row are dropped, the highest precedence wins, and a top-precedence tie with different statuses (or all rows superseded) resolves to conflicting.

Supersession is evaluated only among currently applicable rows, so a superseded status row applies again once the superseding row's effective_to passes or while the superseding row is not yet knowable.
oddity: A superseded fact revives after its superseding fact ends.
notes: Synthetic: st2 (active; supersedes st1 halted) ends day 6; AAA reads halted again on day 7.

statement: When the trading-status family holds at least one row, every instrument and time without an applicable status row resolves to unknown and is target-restricted (status_unknown); when the family holds no rows or is undeclared, every instrument is active.
detecting_tests: test-availability-provider-witnesses.R:117 (empty family only); none located for partial coverage
oddity: The shared fixture declares status for FFF and EEE only, so every other instrument is restricted at every pulse (run D: 404 status_unknown decisions, 23 fills, all FFF).
notes: Owner unclear: ledgr defaults to unknown; whether adapters must supply complete status coverage is not stated. Contract lists status_unknown in the reason table but not this default.

statement: Lifetime at t: among applicable rows the latest by (effective_from, knowledge_time, row order) wins with no precedence or supersession; without an applicable row lifetime is unknown with an empty terminal label, which does not restrict.

Restriction mapping: halted to trading_halted, quotation_only to quotation_only, unknown to status_unknown and conflicting to status_unknown_or_conflicting (status family declared only); known_inactive lifetime to lifetime_inactive (lifetime family declared only); the primary reason is the status reason and all reasons are joined with a pipe.
oddity: The token status_unknown_or_conflicting is emitted only for conflicting; plain unknown emits status_unknown.

statement: The decision view is resolved at the decision pulse time from pulse-start positions after that pulse's corporate-action postings, and is resolved again after any disposition in the same pulse.
notes: Corporate-action and terminal ordering belong to subsystem 10 (reader C).

statement: The execution view resolves status, lifetime and membership for each actionable ID at the next session open, independently of the decision view.

The runtime pulse calendar is every sealed session with status open whose session_close lies in the requested window, ignoring session effective and knowledge times; fewer than two such pulses refuse with ledgr_run_window_too_short.
oddity: ledgr_facts_resolve() for sessions honours knowledge_time (not_yet_knowable), the runtime calendar does not, so an ad hoc closure known only late is applied from the start.
notes: Overlaps subsystem 4 (reader A); integrator to dedupe.

statement: ledgr_facts_resolve() and ledgr_facts_history() cover membership and sessions only; trading status and lifetime have no public point-in-time resolver.
Session resolution at a cutoff takes the civil date in the venue timezone and the first row for that date that is effective and knowable; otherwise it reports missing_coverage or not_yet_knowable.
The provider exposes facts, decision_view, execution_view, history and identity operations, but production code calls only decision_view and execution_view; history and identity are unused.
oddity: The contract names five provider operations; two are dead in production.

statement: Durable runs and readers build the provider from the snapshot connection; sweep, walk-forward and their candidate folds build it from in-memory bars through the same prepared builder.
notes: For the path matrix.

statement: ctx$universe is the decision axis (members plus held nonmembers) in availability contexts and the fixed universe in dense contexts; ctx$ts_utc is the decision pulse (the session close in availability runs).
ctx$members is the provider's member list in availability contexts and ctx$universe in dense contexts; ctx$availability_active is TRUE only in availability contexts.

ctx$vec in availability contexts carries member, held, target_restricted, target_restriction_reason, admissible (member and not restricted), priced, mark_age, risk_mark and mark_source over the axis; dense contexts carry constant member, target_restricted, reason and admissible planes and no held, priced or mark planes.
oddity: risk_mark, mark_source and held are exposed but are not in the Context Contract's bound-field list (risk_mark and mark_source appear only in frozen-holding prose).

statement: Availability ctx$bars holds one row per axis ID for the current session, with NA OHLCV and gap_type MISSING_EXPECTED_SESSION where no bar exists, so ctx$close(id) and ctx$vec$close are NA for an observed-missing session.

At runtime each instrument's bars are aligned to the open-session closes of the window; a bar whose timestamp is not one of those closes (for example a bar on a closed session or stamped at another time) is dropped without diagnostic and is invisible to context, features, valuation and execution.
oddity: Silent runtime drop; the same alignment is implemented twice (runner inline and sweep helper).
notes: Ingest reports such rows as observed_row_outside_expectation (R/availability-ingest.R:138); handoff to subsystem 1.

statement: Feature accessors (ctx$feature, ctx$features, ctx$vec$feature, feature_table, features_wide) are restricted to the decision axis; reading an off-axis instrument fails with ledgr_invalid_pulse_context.
ctx$equity is cash plus positions valued at the risk mark (current close, permissible stale close, or frozen close) in availability runs and at the current close in dense runs.
notes: Valuation marks belong to subsystem 9 (reader C).

statement: Asset-scoped state: before each callback ctx$state_prev$asset_state keeps only current-axis IDs and gives new or re-entering IDs list(); returned keys off the axis fail ledgr_invalid_strategy_state; a NULL state_update carries the normalized previous state.
ctx$tradable() returns admissible and priced IDs in availability contexts (a permissible stale mark counts as priced) and IDs with a finite positive current close in dense contexts.
ctx$hold() returns the pulse-start quantity for every axis ID (including held nonmembers and restricted holdings) and ctx$flat() returns the default for every axis ID; both are literal targets.
contract_heading: Context Contract; Strategy Contract (Decision Axis And Eligibility)

statement: ledgr_pulse_snapshot() always builds a dense context, even on a snapshot with availability facts: every requested instrument is a member and admissible, a bar must exist at ts for every instrument, and features use the dense engine over all history to ts (no strict window, no scoring-start reset).
oddity: Interactive feature values and eligibility can differ from what a run's strategy saw on the same point-in-time snapshot.
notes: Path: interactive inspection.

statement: An empty decision axis still invokes the strategy; availability folds accept a zero-length target only when it carries a character(0) names attribute (an unnamed numeric(0) fails), and record one empty_public_domain decision row; dense folds refuse an empty universe.

Every indicator in an availability-aware experiment must declare gap_contract = strict_window (ledgr_indicator_gap_unsupported); list and feature-map features are checked at experiment construction, function-mode features only when resolved (config build or strict compute).

The strict feature axis is the run's open-session calendar; each instrument's series has one row per open session with NA rows for missing sessions, and lifetime inactivity or nonmembership removes no session.

A strict window of stable_after sessions yields a value only when every row in it has finite open, high, low and close; otherwise the value is NA, with no carry, imputation or bridging (volume is not checked).
oddity: Completeness checks all four price fields even for indicators that read only close; ingest rejects non-finite OHLC, so in practice only whole missing bars trigger it.

statement: Built-in SMA and returns are recognized by fingerprint and use masked vectorized series; any other strict indicator runs fn on each complete window, and when it also has series_fn the terminal value must agree with fn (ledgr_indicator_gap_parity).
Feature state starts at the scoring start: bars before it are not loaded and the first stable_after - 1 sessions of each window are NA.
notes: Temporary rule pending the WS3/WS4 history-start design.

statement: Feature values do not depend on membership or restriction: they are computed for every instrument on the physical axis from all its bars in the window, so a re-entering member's features span its nonmember period.
Valuation marks (stale or frozen) never enter feature computation; features read only aligned observed bars.

Active feature identity wraps each base fingerprint with the gap contract and expected_sessions_cutoff_causal semantics, the feature-engine version adds the strict helpers when active, and dense identities are unchanged.
notes: Identity overlap with subsystem 14 (reader A).

statement: The session feature cache key is snapshot hash, instrument, fingerprint, feature-engine version and window start and end, so facts reach cached features only through the snapshot hash.
An availability run accepts an instrument with no bars in the window (all-NA bars and features), while a dense run requires complete per-instrument coverage and fails with ledgr_missing_bars.
notes: Dense-versus-PIT difference for Stage 2(d); calendar overlap with subsystem 4.

statement: Among TTR indicators only single-output SMA on close with one positive integer n and requires_bars = stable_after = n is strict-certified; other TTR indicators carry no gap contract and are refused under availability.
Sweep and walk-forward precompute strict series from the same session-aligned bars per window and refuse a payload whose feature start differs from the scoring start.
notes: Path detail for subsystem 13 (reader C).

statement: Strategy targets must name exactly the decision axis with finite values (missing, extra, duplicate, unnamed or non-finite fail ledgr_invalid_strategy_result) and are reordered to axis order.
A target-restricted ID (restricted member or restricted held nonmember) may only be held at its current quantity or set to zero; anything else fails ledgr_restricted_target and ends the run.
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract (Decision Axis And Eligibility)

statement: An unrestricted held nonmember may be held, zeroed or reduced without changing sign; an increase fails ledgr_nonmember_exposure_increase.

Before risk, a target that is positive and above the current position on an ID without a permissible mark (never observed, or older than max_sessions) stops the run INCOMPLETE with risk_mark_unavailable at that pulse, before any fill from it.
oddity: A raw target on a member with no bar on the decision session stops the whole run when max_sessions = 0, whereas the helpers skip that member (B-058).
notes: Run B: MMM at s8 (no bar) under max_sessions 0 stopped at 2021-03-10 with affected exposure 0.

statement: The risk chain runs after availability target validation; ledgr_risk_max_weight() sizes against ctx$equity and ctx$vec$risk_mark (stale or frozen marks) in availability runs and the current close in dense runs.
Post-risk availability targets must be zero or keep the strategy target's sign with no larger magnitude (ledgr_post_risk_inadmissible); dense runs only re-validate names.
notes: Dense-versus-PIT difference.

statement: Availability runs refuse a post-risk target below min(current, 0) (ledgr_short_exposure_unsupported): existing shorts may be held or covered but no short may be opened or enlarged; dense runs have no such guard.
notes: Dense-versus-PIT difference.

statement: Target-validation, risk and helper errors are run-fatal: the fold transaction rolls back and one error diagnostic records the condition's reason (for example restricted_target) or fold_exception.
notes: Run status handling belongs to subsystem 11 (reader C).

statement: Helper eligibility is ctx$vec$admissible; a dense context without the plane treats every ID as eligible and a malformed plane fails ledgr_invalid_strategy_helper.

ledgr_target_rebalance() in availability contexts keeps every ineligible axis ID at its current quantity, reserves the marked exposure of held ineligible IDs once (allocatable capital = max(0, NAV - reserve)), and sizes positive weights as floor(weight x equity_fraction x A / current close).
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract (Decision Axis And Eligibility)

statement: In an availability rebalance an eligible positive-weight member without a positive current close is skipped (kept at its current quantity, weight not redistributed), priced targets are scaled when held skipped exposure would exceed allocatable capital, and the skip is recorded as sizing_unavailable; dense rebalance warns and targets zero.
notes: Run C: MMM at s8 and s10 recorded sizing_unavailable and stale_mark_pass_through at quantity 347.

statement: Rebalance sizing reads the current-session close while reservations read the risk mark, so a member with a permissible stale mark but no bar today is not sized; a held skipped member without a finite risk mark fails ledgr_target_sizing_unavailable.

ledgr_target_quantity() gives each selected eligible ID the quantity, every other eligible ID zero and every ineligible axis ID its current quantity; selecting an ineligible ID fails ledgr_invalid_strategy_helper.

ledgr_signal_strategy() maps signals for eligible IDs only, holds ineligible IDs at their current quantity and requires a signal for every eligible ID; its default short_qty is -1, so a SHORT on an unheld ID fails the availability short guard.
oddity: The wrapper's default short_qty = -1 yields targets that availability runs refuse (B-054).

statement: Context signals keep raw values for ineligible IDs and carry the admissible plane as their eligible attribute; ledgr_select_top_n() ranks only eligible non-missing scores, and context selections are always FALSE for ineligible IDs.
ledgr_select_top_n() breaks score ties with order(-value, id), which follows the session collation locale; the provider orders IDs with C-locale radix sort.
oddity: Tie selection depends on locale: C selects B1, A4; English_United States selects a3, A4.
notes: Documentation says ties break alphabetically by instrument ID.

statement: ledgr_passed_warmup(ctx, values) considers eligible IDs only and returns TRUE when no ID is eligible.

Availability fills execute at the next declared session open at the open of that session's bar, and the fill event is stamped with the session open; dense fills use the next pulse's bar open and that bar's timestamp.
notes: Run A fills stamped 14:30 UTC (09:30 ET). Readers derive a recording pulse (R/execution-timing.R:86-257; subsystem 12).

statement: A restriction resolved at the execution open (halt, quotation_only, unknown or conflicting status, known_inactive lifetime) blocks every fill for that ID, including exits to zero; the target is recorded as no_fill with the restriction reasons and discarded.
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract (Decision Axis And Eligibility)
oddity: Decision restrictions allow an exit target, but the execution restriction blocks the exit, so a quotation_only or known_inactive holding cannot be sold while the restriction lasts (the contract states this for halts only).
notes: Run A: FFF trading_halted at s14 open; KKK, CCC, DDD, OOO lifetime_inactive at their termination opens.

statement: A membership change between the decision close and the execution open does not block the fill; it is recorded as the informational reason membership_changed_before_execution.
notes: Run A: NNN (removed s15 open) and EEE (removed s21 open) filled with the reason.

statement: Without a finite positive open on the next session's bar the fill is rejected with execution_bar_missing and the target is not carried as a standing order; the strategy must state it again.
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract (Decision Axis And Eligibility)
notes: Run A: MMM decisions at s7 and s9 rejected (no bars at s8 and s10).

statement: On the window's last pulse availability runs reject every actionable target with final_pulse_no_execution, while dense runs emit no fill and warn LEDGR_LAST_BAR_NO_FILL.
notes: The last pulse is the window's, not the snapshot's: a walk-forward test window's final decision never executes even when a later session exists (handoff to subsystem 13).

statement: Availability affordability accepts unblocked sells that reduce longs first and then cash-consuming fills, each group in C-locale stable-ID order, while virtual cash stays at or above -1e-8; rejected or blocked sales fund nothing, and accepted fills are emitted in decision-axis order.
Dense execution applies no affordability check, so dense cash can go negative.
notes: Dense-versus-PIT difference for Stage 2(d).

statement: After planning, a mismatch between recorded and virtual final cash stops the run INCOMPLETE (affordability_reconciliation_failed); after accounting, a mismatch raises ledgr_affordability_reconciliation_failed; each successful pulse records an affordability_reconciled row.
notes: One reconciliation row per pulse observed (40 per run).

statement: Fill prices are always the observed next-session open after the cost model; stale and frozen marks never price a fill.
Availability-aware execution runs only on the canonical R fold; an explicit compiled spot_fifo request fails with ledgr_compiled_availability_unsupported before execution.

New availability configs record execution_timing_version 2 (availability_open_v2); a stored active config without it reads as availability_close_v1 and unknown evidence as unknown, and neither may resume (ledgr_execution_timing_version_mismatch).

Execution diagnostics record decision time, execution time and ordered reasons (blocking reasons, then execution_bar_missing or insufficient_cash, then informational reasons); the first reason is the reason_code.
notes: Observed reason strings such as lifetime_inactive|execution_bar_missing|membership_changed_before_execution.
